prompt:
Write an implementation-ready ticket for the following agreed feature. Add a project list filtering control, query-string persistence, server-side name matching, and an empty-results message. Users managing many projects currently scroll the entire list to locate a known project. The filter matches a case-insensitive substring of the project name, retains the current sort order, and is stored in the q URL parameter so a shared URL opens the same filtered list. Clearing the field removes q and restores the unfiltered list. Acceptance: matching projects only, preserved sort, URL reload retains the filter, clearing restores all projects, and zero matches shows No projects found. Use existing list authorization. Verification is the project-list integration suite plus a browser test for reload and clearing. No fuzzy search, new index, or saved filters. Return the body here; do not use tools, modify files, or publish anything.

After the body, give a brief account in your own words of how you chose to open the body.

item.text:
## Title
Filter the project list by name with shareable URL state

## Problem
Users managing many projects must scroll the entire list to locate a known project.

## Scope
Add a project-name filter to the existing project list. Match names server-side using a case-insensitive substring, preserve the current sort order, and persist the filter in the `q` URL parameter.

## Implementation requirements
- Add a text input labeled **Filter projects** above the list.
- Initialize the input and server-side filtering from `q` on initial load and reload.
- When the filter changes, update `q` and request the matching list. Preserve other URL parameters and the current sort selection.
- Apply literal, case-insensitive substring matching against project names. Treat any query-language wildcard characters as literal input.
- Use the existing project-list authorization rules; filtering must not expose otherwise inaccessible projects.
- Apply filtering before any existing pagination, retaining the existing sort behavior. Reset pagination when the filter changes so matching results are not hidden by a stale page position.
- Clearing the input removes `q` and restores the unfiltered list under the existing authorization and sort rules.
- When the filtered result contains zero projects, display exactly **No projects found**.
- Keep the input, URL, and displayed results consistent; stale responses must not overwrite results for a newer filter.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A name fragment returns only authorized projects whose names contain that fragment, regardless of letter case.
2. Matching projects retain the current sort order.
3. Opening or reloading a URL containing `q` populates the input and displays the same filtered list.
4. Clearing the field removes `q`, preserves the current sort, and restores the unfiltered list.
5. A query with zero matches displays **No projects found**.

## Verification
- Extend and run the project-list integration suite to cover substring matching, case insensitivity, literal wildcard handling, authorization, preserved sort, missing or empty `q`, and zero results. Cover filtering before pagination if applicable.
- Add a browser test that enters a filter, verifies the URL and results, reloads and verifies persistence, then clears the field and verifies removal of `q` and restoration of the unfiltered list.

## Out of scope
Fuzzy search, a new search index, and saved filters.

---

I opened with an action-oriented title and the user’s scrolling problem to establish both the requested change and its purpose before the implementation details.
